questions.q: How does FACTORY differ from CUSTOM in vtxtable?
options: FACTORY works only for digital systems
FACTORY sends a number, CUSTOM sends MHz
questions.explain: In FACTORY the VTX uses its built-in table; the frequencies in the FC are for display only.

questions.q: A frequency of 0 in a band line means…
questions.explain: Zero blocks the channel — that's how prohibited frequencies are removed.

questions.q: A neighbor says “I'm on E5”. How do you make sure you don't interfere with each other?
options: Trust the letter — everyone's bands are the same
questions.explain: On different VTXs the band letters and numbers can mean different frequencies. Agree in MHz.

questions.q: The order for changing channels when yours is taken?
options: On all drones and goggles at once
questions.explain: A mass change without testing is a mass problem.

questions.q: The OSD shows one frequency, but the goggles get the picture on another. The cause?
options: The goggles or their receiver module are broken
questions.explain: Load the table made specifically for your VTX model and region.

questions.q: The minimum 5.8 GHz analog channel spacing for flying together:
questions.explain: The signal bandwidth is 20–27 MHz; adjacent channels overlap.

questions.q: +15 dB of VTX power gives roughly this much range:
questions.explain: Range ∝ √P: ×1.41 for every 3 dB, 10^(15/20) ≈ 5.6; 25 → 800 mW is ×32 in power, not in range.

questions.q: Why do pilots at a shared field agree on channels in advance?
options: Adjacent analog channels interfere at close frequencies and high power
Otherwise the VTX won't power on
Channels can only be taken in turn
questions.explain: Spacing and low power on the ground reduce mutual interference.
